synopsis: With M'uru hidden beneath Silvermoon, the kingdom's magisters continue pursuing safe public relief through wardstones, storage vessels, healing foci, and distribution conduits. A stable system capable of reaching the whole population remains elusive, while controlled connection of living recipients directly to M'uru proves immediately effective. Rommath argues that a broken people have the right to seize whatever power can keep them alive, and Astalor devises the colder subjugation method needed to govern M'uru's yield without destroying source or recipient. The resulting martial program develops in parallel with the unfinished public-relief work rather than replacing it. Chosen because of her former relationship to the Light and her capacity to bear what others would not, Liadrin becomes the first person to accept and survive a sustained personal connection to M'uru and the central leader of the new order. She dismisses candidates who disobey calibration or let appetite overrule command, while teaching Falanaras to receive rather than seize the current and to direct enough power to destroy a warded target precisely. Each successful candidate receives an individual governed connection to the captive naaru. Through private conversations and the example of her leadership, Liadrin teaches Falanaras to carry that burden without forgetting how they obtained it, while Theron is drawn to the order's promise of disciplined strength in service to Quel'Thalas. Falanaras and Theron state that they intend to become Blood Knights; Lethira answers, with characteristic sarcasm, that she will stick to her bow. When the Blood Knights are founded, Falanaras and Theron take the oath while Lethira continues in the ranger's path, and Falanaras emerges steadied rather than absolved, proud of the order he has chosen while fully aware that its foundation remains a wound.
title: Chapter 11: The First Blood Knights
